# ConfirmDialog

Asks the reader to confirm an action.

```tsx
import { ConfirmDialog } from '@kafka/react'
```

## When to use it

- Before actions that are hard to undo.

## When not to

- For routine actions that can be undone.

## Examples

### Destructive action

In the `danger` tone, focus starts on Cancel and a click outside does not close the dialog.

```tsx
<Demo />
```

## Props

| Prop | Type | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `open` (required) | `boolean` |  |  |
| `onOpenChange` (required) | `(open: boolean) => void` |  |  |
| `title` (required) | `string` |  |  |
| `description` (required) | `ReactNode` |  | What will happen, in a sentence. Say the consequence, not "Are you sure?". |
| `onConfirm` (required) | `() => void` |  | Called when the person confirms. The dialog closes afterwards. |
| `confirmLabel` | `string` |  |  |
| `cancelLabel` | `string` |  |  |
| `tone` | `'default' \| 'danger'` | `'default'` | `danger` is for actions that destroy something: focus starts on Cancel, and a click outside does not close the dialog. |

## Accessibility

- Built on Modal.
- In the `danger` tone focus starts on Cancel and a click outside does not close it, so the destructive action takes a deliberate step.
- The confirm button repeats the action ("Eliminar relato"), not "Aceptar".

## Content

- Say what will be lost.
